---

**Measured, not inferred.** `meetings.ts:465-489` and `checkin.ts:340-373` both re-implement `v_student_participation`'s expression in TypeScript: same summing, same `Math.max(expectedCt - excusedCt, 1)` denominator floor, same `Math.round(x*10)/10` rounding. A change to the view (W4's file) silently desynchronises both. **Not a bug today** — the gate verified all three agree at `d5d420a`. **Do not fix inside T162**; that packet forbids editing `meetings.ts` and the consolidation touches W1's `checkin.ts` too, so it needs its own row and an ownership call. Task Name: T507 — The login card overflows the viewport on every phone narrower than ~400px
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T507`

**Type / provenance:** Bug (responsive) — **found by the `layout-measurement` skill on its first run**

**Title:** The login card overflows the viewport on every phone narrower than ~400px

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-05 — MEASURED in real Chromium, not read from source**

---

`LoginPage.tsx:275` renders `<Card width={400} maxWidth="100%" padding={6}>`. **The author wrote the defensive `maxWidth` and it does nothing** — measured overflow by viewport: **320px → 40px · 360px → 20px · 375px → 13px · 390px → 5px · 414px and wider → 0**. So it affects most phones and worsens as the screen narrows; an iPhone SE is the worst case. **Presence-checked in the same run** (3 buttons, 2 inputs still rendered), so this is a real overflow and not the deleted-content artifact T325 caught. **Mechanism proven by walking the ancestor chain, not inferred:** the card is `rect=400 css-width=400px max-width=100%`, and its parent `.astryx-stack vertical` is **itself 400px with `max-width: none`** — so `100%` resolves against a box the card already sized, making the constraint a no-op. The first genuinely constrained ancestor is `.astryx-center` at 390px. **This is T325's exact mechanism on a second surface** (`maxWidth="100%"` resolving against an unconstrained parent, measured there as *no change*) — see T325's verification-log entry before packeting. **Candidate direction, not a prescription:** `maxWidth={400}` + `width="100%"` so the card fills the available width up to 400 rather than demanding 400 — but **measure it, do not assume it**; T325's obvious fix measured as a no-op. **No regression test is possible in jsdom** (no layout), so evidence is a before/after measurement, per the `layout-measurement` skill. **Not W2's surface** — `src/pages/login/**` belongs to no active workflow; needs an owner assignment before it is packeted.

Task Name: T612 — `mutation-replay`'s `replay.py` reports a genuine red replay as `UNTRUSTWORTHY: the mutated run executed no tests`
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T612`

**Type / provenance:** Defect (shared tooling — **the anti-vacuity check itself is unreliable**) — found by T609's checker

**Title:** `mutation-replay`'s `replay.py` reports a genuine red replay as `UNTRUSTWORTHY: the mutated run executed no tests`

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-06**

---

**Measured.** `.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/replay.py` printed `UNTRUSTWORTHY: the mutated run executed no tests` for a run whose **own captured output** showed `Failed Tests 1` with a real assertion failure (`expected [Function] to throw an error`, `ScheduleMeetingsDialog.test.tsx:1156`). Its summary parser read `failed=0 passed=0 skipped=56` off a vitest output shape it mishandles — a focused `-t` run, where the counter line reports skips separately. **Why this matters more than a parser bug:** mutation replay is this project's primary defence against a test that cannot fail, and the constitution leans on it (*"A gate that only reads is worth much less than one that runs"*). A false `UNTRUSTWORTHY` teaches agents to distrust and re-do valid replays — or worse, to accept the verdict and discard the evidence. T609's checker caught it only because it refused the tool's verdict and re-ran the mutation strictly by hand. **Shape:** fix the parser for the focused-run output shape, and make it fail loudly on an output it cannot parse rather than emitting a confident wrong verdict — the same rule T512 carries for ledger counts. **Cross-cutting; `.claude/skills/**` is W10's or the boss's surface, not W3's.**

Task Name: T512 — `WORKFLOWS.md`'s open-row counts are hand-recounted from the document itself; derive them from the ledger with a script instead
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T512`

**Type / provenance:** Debt (process) — **filed 2026-08-05 on the owner's suggestion during PR #89 review**

**Title:** `WORKFLOWS.md`'s open-row counts are hand-recounted from the document itself; derive them from the ledger with a script instead

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-05**

---

**Filed because hand-recounting produced two wrong numbers in one PR.** `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`'s assignment table carries an open-row count per workflow. PR #89 recomputed those counts by reading `WORKFLOWS.md` — which is the artifact under repair — and shipped **two** defects the owner caught in review. (1) The helper treated `NARROWED` as a closed status, so T333 was silently dropped from every count and W9 read `3 — all human gates` while the same cell described T333's machine-workable ETL half. (2) The helper split the file into sections on `^## (W\d+) — `; W10 is the **last** workflow section, so its section ran to EOF and swallowed the Coordination-rules block-allocation table that follows, counting `T333`, `T600-699` and `T700-799` as W10 rows — W10 went 8 → 9 when the true figure was **6** (8 listed, T157 and T301 merged). Both defects are the same class: a count derived from prose, where a parsing miss produces a plausible number instead of an error. **The owner's framing, which is the fix:** *"the ledger is the only place a row's status actually lives, so counts belong derived from it — even a scripted count would beat hand-recounting a doc that four machines are appending to."* **Shape of the work:** a script reading `docs/swarm/task-ledger.md`'s pipe table (ID in column 1, Status in column 8), mapping each row ID to a workflow via the block allocation, and emitting open counts per workflow. Two requirements carried from the failures above — it must treat `NARROWED` as **open**, and it must **fail loudly** rather than return a number when a row ID maps to no workflow block or a status string matches none of the known keywords. A count that cannot be computed must say so; that is the same rule the `mutation-replay` skill enforces. Whether it runs in CI or by hand before a table edit is open. Suggested Allowed Files: `scripts/**`, `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`. **MEASURED 2026-08-05, and it raises the bar for this row: the table is NOT column-consistent, so "Status is column 8" is not a safe parse.** Splitting all 278 `|Tnnn|` rows on unescaped pipes gives **248 rows with the header's 10 columns, and 30 that disagree** — 2 with 9, 21 with 11, 6 with 12, 1 with 13. Found while updating T604 by column index: the patch asserted 10 columns and aborted rather than writing to the wrong cell. **A positional parser must therefore locate `Status` by header name and FAIL LOUDLY on any row whose column count does not match the header — never index blindly**, which is the same "a miss must error, not return a plausible number" requirement this row already carries. Normalising the 30 rows is the obvious companion fix and may be the cheaper half.

Task Name: T705 — The schema and all four consuming views are multi-team; the roster UI and write path are still single-team, and three roster filters still scope on the legacy `students.team_id`
Description:

**Title:** The schema and all four consuming views are multi-team; the roster UI and write path are still single-team, and three roster filters still scope on the legacy `students.team_id`

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-06, restated the same day. Source-verified. NOT blocked.**

---

**Scope, all verified in source on `main` and independent of any database:** (1) `student_teams` is written by **nothing** in the repo except the one-time backfill at `20260721000000_student_teams.sql:37` — verified across `src/`, `supabase/functions`, `scripts/` and every migration; no trigger, no edge function. Its sole application access is a `.select('team_id')` at `loaders/students.ts:482`. (2) `makeCreateStudent` (`:279`) and `makeUpdateStudent` (`:307`) write `students.team_id` only, so changing a student's team updates the badge and never the membership. (3) `StudentDialog.tsx` is single-select (one `teamId: string`), while `student_teams` is `primary key (student_id, team_id)` + `left_on` and the views are built for dual membership. (4) **Three roster filters do FUNCTIONAL single-team scoping** — `endMeeting.ts:340` (omits a dual-team student from the End Meeting roster entirely), `kiosk.ts:324`, `kiosk.ts:458` — the T187 defect class, live in three places. Note `kiosk.ts`'s `loadActiveStudentTeams` is misleadingly named: `queryActiveStudentTeams` (`:238-240`) selects from **`students`**. (5) Astryx ships `MultiSelector`, so the UI half is unblocked. ⚠️ **PRODUCTION DATA IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW AND WAS REMOVED FROM IT.** Three data-derived causes were filed and each was disproved by measurement: *students missing membership rows* (owner's query: **0** uncovered), *memberships pointing at archived teams* (**all 23 live**), and *most students inactive* (`kpi_views.sql:207` defines the strip's count as `count(*) from students where is_active`, which reads 22). A fourth — the observed Hours-by-team anomaly being season-scoping — was **not** pursued. **The owner then noted the database predates recent updates and has been through resets and manual edits, so it cannot testify about current code at all.** The dual membership found on George-Student (`test` + `Polytechnic Puzzle Pieces`, explaining 23 rows across 22 students) is therefore treated as development debris, not as a defect. **The earlier "students see an empty portal" severity claim is WITHDRAWN** — that student's `teamIds` scope to two teams with no matching upcoming events, so an empty Next up may simply be correct. **No user-facing defect is claimed by this row.** It is debt: the D018 work, scoped.

Task Name: T806 — `events`/`event_sessions` RLS scopes by the legacy `students.team_id`, so a dual-team student never receives their second team's events
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T806`

**Type / provenance:** Bug (RLS scoping divergence) — **filed 2026-08-07 while closing T199**

**Title:** `events`/`event_sessions` RLS scopes by the legacy `students.team_id`, so a dual-team student never receives their second team's events

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-07 (item 20). Needs a migration → OWNER APPLIES (item 16). Zero impact today.**

---

**Found while building T199's real `events` read, and T199 is what makes it observable** — before it the page had no rows at all, so nothing could be missing from them. `20260717000002_rls.sql:153-161`, verbatim: ```create policy own_or_linked_read on events for select to authenticated using (exists (select 1 from students s where s.id in (select my_student_ids()) and (events.team_ids is null or s.team_id = any(events.team_ids))));``` — and `event_sessions` (`:180-188`) inherits the identical test through `event_id`. **Both read the LEGACY single `students.team_id` column.** T187 (landed) moved `StudentHome` onto ACTIVE `student_teams` memberships (`StudentScope.teamIds`), so the page and the policy now scope by different sources. **They disagree for exactly one shape of user:** a dual-team student. An event scoped to `team_ids = {their SECOND team}` satisfies the page's `isEventInTeamScope` but is filtered out by RLS before it ever reaches the client — that student silently misses their second team's meetings, live check-in and sign-up opportunities. This is the SAME defect T187 fixed on the page side, still live one layer down. **Not the same as the withdrawn T804** — that row wrongly claimed `v_student_participation` scoped off `students.team_id` (it had already been migrated onto `student_teams` by `20260722000000_membership_views.sql`). These are RLS POLICIES, not views, and the grep is unambiguous: no later migration drops or replaces either policy. **Read from the policy text, NOT measured against a live database** — the text is unambiguous on this point, but the measurement was not run and this row should not be closed claiming it was. **Zero impact today:** every student in the system is single-team, and for them the two sources name the same team. **Scope, not yet designed:** a new additive migration replacing both policies' `s.team_id = any(...)` test with an ACTIVE `student_teams` membership test (`left_on is null`), matching what `membership_views.sql` already did for the views. Constitution item 10 forbids editing the applied `20260717000002_rls.sql`, so this is a NEW file using `drop policy if exists` + `create policy`, the route `20260720000001_avatar_storage.sql` already establishes for policy replacement. Needs an RLS assertion suite (the `sql` CI job now runs 12 steps) proving a dual-team fixture student sees BOTH teams' events. **Owner applies the migration (item 16).** Also check `attendance`/`rsvps` policies for the same pattern before designing — this row only verified `events` and `event_sessions`.

Task Name: T807 — Two loaders still apply the `greatest(x, 1)` floor T509 removed, and three row types still declare `participation_pct` non-nullable
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T807`

**Type / provenance:** Bug (T509 fallout, two stale aggregates + three wrong types) — **filed 2026-08-07 while closing T199**

**Title:** Two loaders still apply the `greatest(x, 1)` floor T509 removed, and three row types still declare `participation_pct` non-nullable

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-07 (item 20). TypeScript-only — no migration.**

---

**Found while writing T199's own participation aggregate, by looking for an in-repo expression to reuse rather than inventing one (constitution item 3).** T509 (`20260806000000_met01_explicit_marks.sql`, APPLIED) replaced `v_student_participation`'s `round(100.0 * present_ct / greatest(expected_ct - excused_ct, 1), 1)` with an explicit `case when ... = 0 then null else round(...) end`, precisely so that a student whose every mark is `excused` stops reporting a fabricated `0.0%` and reports NULL (which the UI already renders as an em dash). **Two loaders re-apply the removed floor when they aggregate a dual-team student's per-team rows:** `loaders/meetings.ts:516` (`Math.max(expectedCt - excusedCt, 1)`, in `aggregateParticipationRows`) and `loaders/checkin.ts:375` (identical expression). Both comments cite the view's expression as their authority — that citation is now stale, and the citation being stale is what makes this hard to spot: the code looks correct and says why. **Behavioural consequence:** an all-excused student renders `—` on `ParticipationTab`/`StudentHome` (which read the view directly) and `0%` on `MeetingsList`/check-in (which go through these aggregates). Two screens, two different answers, for the case T509 exists to fix. **Three row types are also wrong at the type level:** `meetings.ts:283`, `checkin.ts:239` and `reports.ts:221` each declare `participation_pct: number` while the view can now return SQL NULL. `reports.ts`/`checkin.ts` happen to survive it (a null flows through the mapper and `ParticipationTab.tsx:830-831` renders `—`), so this is a lie in the types rather than a crash — but it is the lie that lets the two stale aggregates above look fine. T199's own `StudentHomeParticipationDbRow` types it `number | null` and returns `null` for the whole metric when the denominator is zero; that is the shape to converge on. **Consider widening `StudentParticipationMetric.participationPct` to `number | null`** — the shape is shared by `MeetingsList.tsx`, `StudentMeetingView.tsx`, `ParentHome.tsx` and `StudentHome.tsx` plus their tests, which is why T199 did not do it inline (item 25). **Verified before filing:** all five call sites read directly, and no later migration re-introduces the floor. **Not a migration** — T509's SQL is correct and applied; this is entirely TypeScript catching up to it.

This is the same dangling-forward-reference shape that left T199 unfixed for weeks, and the same placeholder-default family as T155 (`CoachHome`), T176 (`StudentHome`) and T181 (`ParentHome`); **T168 is the sweep that should have caught it and did not — worth a line in T168 rather than a separate finding.** **The computation already exists and must not be re-derived** (constitution item 3): `getUnansweredRsvpCount` (`OutreachList.tsx:1459`), signature `(sessions, rsvps, studentIds) => number`, already counts a `scheduled` session with no matching `rsvps` row per student. **Do NOT scope this as a one-line swap.** That signature is the whole difficulty: `SideNav` currently takes no data at all, so wiring it means giving the app-shell nav a real loader plus the viewer's resolved student ids — a new data dependency in the chrome, which is why T038 correctly declined to do it inline. Expect **STANDARD**, and expect the seam design (does the badge load its own data, or does `AppShell` thread it down?) to be the actual decision. **OWNERSHIP IS OPEN — the owner must assign it.** `src/components/nav/**` belongs to no workflow; the data is outreach (**W2**, CLOSED, 0 open rows) and the mount point is the shell (**W5**/W10 territory). Same situation as **T507**, which is parked in the WORKFLOWS table as *unowned surface* awaiting exactly this call. Filed in W1's block because W1 found it, **not** as an ownership claim.
